query: How do core (LLM) + ordinary (ABM) users' opinions on abortion rights evolve on a Twitter-like platform after the trigger news that the Supreme Court overturns Roe v. Wade (HiSim hybrid social-movement replication)?
method_notes: 技术报告 §5.7 社会运动 case 导入：模拟与真实两条 14 轮序列由 build_from_techreport.py 从图表源码逐点提取并回读校验；真值锚是同期真实 Twitter 群体情绪。本工作台不重跑该管线——移植代码 model.py/reporting.py 保留，早先 4 步真实 LLM 验证的数字保留在报告末节。

implementation_refs.title: Mou et al. (2024) — Unveiling the Truth and Facilitating Change: Towards Agent-based Large-scale Social Movement Simulation (HiSim, ACL 2024 Findings)
implementation_refs.takeaway: The paper this study ports. Hybrid design: a small set of 'core' users driven by LLMs (post/retweet/reply/like on a Twitter-like env) plus numerous 'ordinary' users driven by deductive agent-based bounded-confidence models; opinions are read off each core user's produced tweet (att2score: sign(stance)·|sentiment|). Directly maps to hisim.hybrid_decision (core LLM branch + ordinary BCM branch) and the env 'mirror'.

implementation_refs.title: Deffuant, Neau, Amblard & Weisbuch (2000) — Mixing beliefs among interacting agents (Advances in Complex Systems 3)
implementation_refs.takeaway: Foundational bounded-confidence (BCM) opinion-dynamics model: agents hold continuous opinions and assimilate toward one another ONLY when their opinions differ by less than a confidence bound; below/above the threshold the population converges to consensus, polarization, or fragmentation. Grounds the ordinary-user rule in model.py (_decide_ordinary: new = x + alpha·(peer−x) for |peer−x| < bc_bound; alpha=0.3, bc_bound=0.1).

facts.claim: The Supreme Court decision Dobbs v. Jackson Women's Health Organization overturned Roe v. Wade on 2022-06-24, ending ~50 years of federally guaranteed abortion access and returning abortion regulation to the states — the exogenous shock that fires as trigger_news.

source.title: Supreme Court overturns constitutional right to abortion (SCOTUSblog)

facts.note: HiSim's ROE ref config sets current_time 2022-06-24 22:00 and trigger_news[0] to this exact event; the study's broadcast N1 is the SocioVerse2-native rendering of that shock.

facts.claim: About 61% of Americans said abortion should be legal in all or most cases (Pew, published 2022-06-13, just before the decision).

source.title: About six-in-ten Americans say abortion should be legal in all or most cases (Pew Research Center)

facts.note: Real-world prior: a pro-rights majority. The synthetic pool seeds opinions uniformly on [-1,1] (see assumption a-uniform-init) rather than skewing +0.22 to match this share — the showcase demonstrates mechanics, not a calibrated electorate; the number frames how the trigger perturbs an already pro-rights-leaning public.

facts.claim: After the decision, 57% of U.S. adults disapproved of the Court's ruling to overturn Roe (43% strongly) while 41% approved (25% strongly); Pew survey of 6,174 adults, 2022-06-27→07-04.

source.title: Majority of Public Disapproves of Supreme Court's Decision to Overturn Roe v. Wade (Pew Research Center)

facts.note: Directional validation target: post-shock aggregate sentiment toward the decision is net negative (disapproval > approval). The study's `bias` metric (mean attitude − neutral) and the pro-rights framing of stances read against this real net-negative reaction.

facts.claim: HiSim's published ROE configuration runs 1000 ordinary ABM users with initial attitudes init_att≈0.87-0.99 (strongly pro-rights), a bounded-confidence alpha=0.3, over max_turns=14 (12h per turn from 2022-06-24).
facts.note: The published scale the showcase downsizes from. alpha=0.3 is carried faithfully; the demo uses 8 core + 12 ordinary and 4 steps instead of 1000 users / 14 turns (assumption a-showcase-scale) to keep the real-LLM run cheap.

assumptions.statement: 本研究轨迹是已发表运行的导入，不是工作台内重跑。
assumptions.rationale: HiSim 需要真实 Twitter 数据与大量 LLM 调用；导入让'与真值对照'的形态立刻可见，代价是该次运行本身不可在此复现（可复现的是导入过程）。

assumptions.statement: 两条序列各自 min-max 归一化，只比形状不比绝对值。
assumptions.rationale: 两者绝对量程不重叠，这是技术报告的既有口径；绝对水平吻合由 ΔBias 单独报告。

assumptions.statement: 相关系数有两个口径：数字化重算 0.783、论文公布 0.758。
assumptions.rationale: 数字化误差所致。报告与论文各自引用对应口径，不混用。

assumptions.statement: 没有逐人面板：论文只公开聚合轨迹。
assumptions.rationale: 个体层证据是单轮回复的对齐指标，不是逐人序列——缺的留空，不补。

assumptions.claim: The showcase runs 8 LLM core users + 12 ordinary ABM users over 4 steps (news fires at step 2), versus HiSim's published 1000 ordinary users over 14 turns. Core/ordinary counts and n_steps are declared adjustable_params (artifact-level, no simulator-code change).
assumptions.rationale: A faithful 1000-user / 14-turn real-LLM run is neither cheap nor necessary to demonstrate the hybrid mechanics (LLM core mirror + BCM ordinary assimilation + trigger-news shock). The small scale exercises the full real-LLM decision path and the endogenous env feedback end-to-end at ~32 core-LLM calls total. Not a published quantity — declared, not sourced.

assumptions.claim: Initial opinions for both core and ordinary users are seeded uniformly at random on [-1,1] (deterministic in seed=42 via the synthetic world builder), NOT loaded from HiSim's real role_desc / init_att data (absent on this server) nor skewed to the +0.22 pro-rights prior implied by Pew's 61% legal-support share.
assumptions.rationale: HiSim's real ROE user_data (role descriptions, follower graph, per-user init_att) is not present in this workspace, so model.load_movement's real path cannot run; the committed bundles use the synthetic _synth world. A uniform prior is the honest neutral default for a mechanics demo — it lets the trigger-news effect and BCM convergence show against a symmetric starting distribution rather than a pre-loaded consensus. Real-data calibration is the natural next /sv-iterate step.
